record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can one develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of sine-Gordon scattering off a non-integrable boundary, despite the fact that the boundary interaction excites many additional modes?

evidence.quote: To this end, it would be nice to develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of the boundary situation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon field theory on the half-line x ≤ 0, with field φ(x,t) governed by the bulk equation
   ∂_t^2 φ − ∂_x^2 φ + sin φ = 0,
together with the one-parameter family of Robin boundary conditions at x = 0,
   ∂_x φ(0,t) = M sin(φ(0,t)/2),
where M ∈ ℝ is a real parameter. For generic M this boundary condition breaks the integrability of the bulk theory, and the scattering of an incoming antikink (or kink) off the boundary excites not only the soliton's translational zero mode but also a host of additional degrees of freedom (boundary-localized modes, breathers, and continuum radiation), so that the outgoing state may consist of various combinations of an antikink, a kink, and one or more breathers depending on the incident velocity and on M.

Problem. Develop an effective collective-coordinate description of antikink/kink scattering off this non-integrable boundary that quantitatively captures the observed reflection, transmission into breathers, and resonance windows. Concretely, exhibit a finite-dimensional reduction of the field dynamics — specifying a moduli ansatz φ(x,t) ≈ Φ(x; q_1(t), …, q_n(t)) and the resulting effective Lagrangian L_eff(q, q̇) — whose solutions reproduce, with controlled accuracy, the scattering outcomes of the full PDE for a wide range of M and incident velocities, including the resonant energy exchange between the soliton translational mode and the modes excited at the boundary.
artifact.status_search_result: Boundary scattering of sine-Gordon solitons under non-integrable Robin boundary conditions has been studied numerically (e.g., showing intricate resonance structures and breather production), and collective-coordinate methods have been successful in related impurity and deformed sine-Gordon problems. However, no published collective-coordinate reduction is reported to give an effective and quantitatively accurate description of sine-Gordon scattering off the non-integrable Robin boundary, due to the many additional modes excited there. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Breaking integrability at the boundary: the sine-Gordon model with Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: An antikink may be reflected into various combinations of an antikink, a kink, and one or more breathers... intricate resonance structures arise from the creation of an intermediate breather whose recollision with the boundary is highly dependent on the breather phase.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the non-integrable Robin boundary problem and complex outgoing states, motivating but not providing an effective collective-coordinate description.

status_evidence.title: Collective coordinate approximation to the scattering of solitons in modified NLS and sine-Gordon models
status_evidence.snippet: Collective coordinate approximations have been used to investigate the validity of soliton scattering in several classes of (1+1) dimensional field theory models.
status_evidence.claim: Collective-coordinate methods exist for bulk deformations of sine-Gordon, but the boundary case with many excited modes is not addressed effectively.
